cumleler: Why does a hearing aid whistle?
The receiver delivers amplified sound into the ear canal.
Some of it escapes through the vent or gaps around the earmold.
The leaked sound reaches the microphone, and the aid amplifies it again.
As the loop feeds itself, a steady whistle appears.
For a new whistle, first check the ear canal with an otoscope.
